subject: social_science
chapter_title: Development: Income, Public Facilities and Sustainability

concepts.title: Different People, Different Developmental Goals
concepts.definition: Each person pictures progress through the lens of their own life situation, so a landless labourer may want regular work and better wages while a prosperous farmer may want higher support prices, and goals of different groups can even conflict.
concepts.key_idea: What is development for one person may be destructive for another, as when a large dam brings electricity to industry but submerges the land of displaced tribals.
question_patterns: why do different persons have different notions of development
give examples of conflicting developmental goals
what may be development for one may be destructive for another explain
list the developmental goals of a landless rural labourer
how do the aspirations of an urban unemployed youth differ from those of a farmer
why can development goals of two groups clash

solution_steps.explain: Place the person in their life situation, such as landless labourer, rain-dependent farmer, urban unemployed youth, or adivasi from the Narmada valley.

Check the aspiration fits the situation: more days of work and better wages for labourers, higher support prices for prosperous farmers, freedom and education for a girl seeking equality with her brother.
Confirm whether one group's gain harms another, such as industrialists wanting more dams while displaced people prefer small check dams or tanks.

concepts.title: Income and Other Goals in Life
concepts.definition: Besides more income, people seek equal treatment, freedom, security and respect, and these non-material goods matter because money cannot buy everything needed for a good life.
concepts.key_idea: A job with lower pay but regular employment may give a stronger sense of security than a highly paid post with no security, showing that people weigh a mix of goals.
question_patterns: why is more income not the only goal of development
give examples where factors other than income are important
how do freedom and security shape job choices
what non material things do people seek besides income
how does paid work affect the dignity of women
explain why material goods are not all that we need

solution_steps.explain: Income and goods bought with money are material; equal treatment, freedom, security and respect are non-material goals.
Compare jobs on pay, regularity, working atmosphere, family time and opportunity to learn to see why income alone cannot rank them.
Confirm the answer treats development as a mix of goals, for example safe environments letting more women take up jobs or run businesses.

concepts.title: Comparing Countries by Per Capita Income
concepts.section: How to Compare Different Countries or States
concepts.definition: Countries are compared using average income, computed by dividing the total income of a country by its total population, and this average is called per capita income.
concepts.key_idea: World Development Reports classify countries by per capita income, placing rich countries far above low-income countries, with India in the low middle income group.
question_patterns: how is per capita income of a country calculated
why is total income not useful for comparing countries
what criterion does the world bank use to classify countries
calculate the per capita income from total income and population
into which income category does india fall
define average income and per capita income

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total income of the country by its total population to get the average income per person

concepts.title: Average Income of a Group of Persons
concepts.definition: The average income of a small group, such as the citizens of a model country, is the sum of all their incomes divided by the number of persons, and averages hide disparities in distribution.
concepts.key_idea: Two countries with identical averages can differ sharply in equity: one with similar incomes for all is preferred to one where most people are poor and one person is extremely rich.
question_patterns: calculate the average income of the citizens from the given table
find the mean monthly income of a group of persons
why do averages hide disparities in income distribution
which of two countries with the same average income is preferred and why
compute the average income for country a and country b
what limitation of averages does the rich and poor country example show

solution_steps.explain: Sum the monthly incomes of every person in the group
solution_steps.compute: total_income = income_1 + income_2 + income_3 + income_4 + income_5

solution_steps.explain: Divide the combined income by the number of persons to get the average

concepts.title: Missing Family Income from the Group Average
concepts.definition: When the average income of a group is known along with all but one member's income, the unknown income equals the group average multiplied by the number of members, minus the sum of the known incomes.
concepts.key_idea: This reversal of the average formula shows how averages constrain every member, as in the textbook case of four families with average income Rs 5000.
question_patterns: find the income of the fourth family given the average income of four families
calculate the missing income when the group average is known
the average per capita income of four families is given find the unknown income
how do you work backwards from an average to a missing value
what is the income of the remaining family if three incomes and the average are known

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the group average by the number of families to get the combined income
Subtract the sum of the known family incomes from the combined income to isolate the missing income

concepts.title: Income and Other Criteria: Kerala versus Haryana
concepts.definition: States with higher per capita income can still lag on health and education, because money cannot buy a pollution-free environment, unadulterated medicines or protection from infectious disease unless the whole community is served.
concepts.key_idea: Haryana has the higher per capita income but Kerala has far lower Infant Mortality and higher literacy and net attendance, so public facilities matter as much as income.
question_patterns: why does kerala have a better human development ranking than haryana
is per capita income alone a useful criterion to compare states
what does infant mortality rate indicate
why is money in your pocket not enough to buy all you need to live well
compare haryana and bihar on literacy and attendance
what are public facilities and why are they needed

solution_steps.explain: Compare per capita income with Infant Mortality Rate, literacy rate and net attendance ratio for Haryana, Kerala and Bihar.
Note that Haryana's higher income coexists with an infant mortality nearly three times Kerala's, showing income is not an adequate indicator.
Confirm the reasoning that collective provision of health, education and clean environment is the cheapest and best way to supply goods markets cannot sell to individuals.

concepts.title: Infant Mortality Rate from Birth and Death Data
concepts.definition: Infant Mortality Rate counts the children who die before completing one year of age for every 1000 live children born in that year, so it is computed from the number of infant deaths and live births.
concepts.key_idea: Kerala's IMR of 6 against Haryana's 28 per 1000 shows how health outcomes diverge even within one country.

find the imr per 1000 live births for a state

how many children per thousand died before one year of age
compare the imr of kerala and haryana

solution_steps.action: scale deaths to a thousand births
solution_steps.explain: Divide the number of infant deaths by the number of live births and multiply by 1000

concepts.title: Net Attendance Ratio of School Children
concepts.definition: The Net Attendance Ratio is the total number of children of the 15-17 year age group attending school expressed as a percentage of all children in that age group.
concepts.key_idea: With about one-third of Bihar's 15-17 year olds out of secondary school, attendance data expose gaps that income averages miss.
question_patterns: calculate the net attendance ratio from enrolment data
find the percentage of children attending secondary school
what does net attendance ratio measure
how many children per hundred in the age group attend school
compute the attendance ratio of a state given school data
why does the attendance ratio matter for development

solution_steps.explain: Divide the number of children attending school by the total children in the age group and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Human Development Index of UNDP
concepts.definition: The Human Development Index published in the Human Development Report ranks countries by health, education and income together, placing people and their well being at the centre of development.
concepts.key_idea: Sri Lanka, a small neighbour, ranks ahead of India, and Nepal and Bangladesh beat India in life expectancy despite lower per capita income, which shows why UNDP uses broader criteria than the World Bank.
question_patterns: how is the undp criterion different from the world bank criterion
what does hdi stand for and what does it measure
which neighbouring countries perform better than india in human development
why is sri lanka ahead of india in human development
what new components have been added to the human development report
why do nepal and bangladesh beat india in life expectancy

solution_steps.explain: HDI combines health (life expectancy), education (literacy, enrolment) and income rather than income alone.
The World Bank classifies by per capita income while UNDP ranks by the broader human development record.
Check the table: Sri Lanka's rank ahead of India, and Nepal and Bangladesh leading on life expectancy despite lower income.

concepts.title: Body Mass Index of Students
concepts.definition: Body Mass Index is a nutrition measure found by dividing a person's weight in kilograms by the square of height in metres, with low values signalling undernourishment and high values overweight.
concepts.key_idea: Recording each student's weight and height, converting centimetres to metres, and computing BMI lets a class screen for undernourished or overweight members without body shaming.
question_patterns: calculate the body mass index from weight and height
find the bmi of a student weighing kilograms and metres tall
how is body mass index computed
what bmi value marks a boy of fifteen as overweight
compute the bmi after converting height from centimeters to meters
why do nutrition scientists use body mass index

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the height in metres by itself
Divide the weight in kilograms by the squared height to get the body mass index

concepts.title: Sustainability of Development and Groundwater Overuse
concepts.definition: Development is sustainable only when future generations can also maintain it, yet about 300 districts have seen groundwater levels fall over four metres in two decades and nearly one-third of the country is overusing its groundwater reserves.
concepts.key_idea: Groundwater overuse concentrates in agriculturally prosperous Punjab and Western U.P., the hard rock plateau areas of central and south India, some coastal areas and fast-growing urban settlements.
question_patterns: why is the issue of sustainability important for development
why is groundwater overused in india
can there be development without overuse of groundwater
which regions show the most groundwater overuse
what does the evidence say about declining water levels
explain the idea that we have borrowed the world from our children

solution_steps.explain: Ask whether the present level and type of development can be maintained for future generations.
Recall 300 districts with water level declines of over 4 metres in 20 years and one-third of the country overusing reserves, rising to 60 per cent in 25 years if current use continues.
Locate overuse in Punjab and Western U.P., central and south Indian hard rock plateaus, coastal belts and growing urban settlements, then judge remedies that restrain extraction.
